about: Expected verdicts of `modelspec lint` for every corpus item, under both profiles. An item is a file (hcl/, json/) or a directory (modules/: a SpecScore project in the SpecScore layout; standalone/: files linted together, with `modules` as --module assignments relative to the item). Every item in the old spelling (entity, property, entity =; format 1.0-draft) is refused, with the error deprecated-spelling (decision 0022, step 4: the old spelling is an error in a module that is being checked). An item is linted with its own directory as the one path named, so every file of it, `modules` assignments included, lies under a named path and is checked; that is the only difference between its verdict and the verdict of its copy in the new spelling, where there is a copy. The warning for a module that is only referred to needs a module supplied from outside every path named, which no item can do (its `modules` are relative to the item), so it is tested in the Go tests of lint. `differs` names the reader whose recorded verdict (testdata/golden) is different, and says why, compared with the verdict of lint without the spelling error (the recorded readers still read the old spelling): specscore is compared with the default profile, the Directory's JSON reader with the publish profile. An item under parts/ is one file of another item, given alone (as an editor or a hook would): `path` is where it is under this directory, and a module is the unit, so its verdict is that of the whole module it belongs to. Parts are not compared with the other readers, which lint a whole project. An item without `differs` must have the same verdict as the reader recorded for it. An item under new/ is the item of the same path in the new spelling (record, field, record =; format 1.0-draft-2). Where `modelspec rewrite` can rewrite every model file of the old item, the copy is what rewrite makes of it, byte for byte (a test checks it). Where it cannot, because a file does not parse, repeats a key in a JSON object, or holds a removed construct or a reserved word (decision 0019), the copy was written by hand: the old words replaced, and for an item whose removed construct was only a part of its purpose (a collection beside records) without it; the old item keeps the construct and so refuses. The items listed in the test as new only have no old twin: they hold both spellings together. Items under new/ are not compared with the other readers, which do not read the new spelling yet; the same goes for new/parts/.

differs.specscore: specscore accepts a property named by a blank string; no property of that name could ever be referenced, so the standard cannot mean it to be valid (spec/core-model.md: names identify)
removed by decision 0019: collection blocks no longer exist (specscore reads them and does not resolve their bind values)
specscore accepts an entity named by the empty string; nothing could ever refer to it, and the Directory's reader refuses the same model in JSON form
specscore resolves a bare entity reference to anything in the entity/component/enum scope without checking the kind; the property's `entity` attribute must name an entity
specscore resolves a bare entity reference to anything in the entity/component/enum scope without checking the kind; the property's `entity` attribute must name an entity
lint accepts integer enum values and specscore refuses them; decision 0013 says an enum constrains a string or an int property, so the standard allows them
specscore ignores attributes whose value is not a plain literal; lint refuses expressions (decision 0009)
specscore ignores attributes it does not know; lint refuses map-style containers (decisions 0007, 0009), and the entity keeps a key naming a property that was never declared
specscore ignores attributes it does not know; the JSON format requires constraints to use supported keys
specscore does not check types; the JSON format requires the type to be in the supported set

differs.directory: the Directory's reader keeps the last of two equal keys; names are unique, and readers disagree on which repeat wins
the Directory's reader takes the last of two equal keys, so it sees a valid `type`; lint refuses the repeat, which other readers resolve the other way
the Directory's reader does not read enums; the format requires enum values to be unique
the Directory's reader does not use keys; a key must name a property
the Directory's reader reads only module.name; the format requires module.id and module.version
the Directory's reader reads only module.name; the format requires module.id and module.version
the Directory's reader accepts any type spelled like a type name, `string[]` included; the standard's type vocabulary has no array types
the Directory's reader checks only that a type is spelled like a type name; the format requires one of the supported types
the Directory's reader reads only entities; the format requires every group to have the shape it defines
the Directory's reader ignores constraints; the format requires them to have valid value types
the Directory's reader accepts any string as the modelspec version; the format defines 1.0-draft

differs.specscore: lint accepts and specscore refuses a qualified reference to a module missing from the referencing module's dependsOn (graph-dependency-direction); that rule is about SpecScore's own module metadata and is not part of ModelSpec, so lint does not apply it
